The only phonological claim is segmental: a 'high, central unrounded vowel' inferred from colonial spellings of place names; the rest is morpheme segmentation and lexical comparison with Taino/Island Carib. Confirms the corpus is c. 50 place names with no accent-marked or spoken data, so the published chapter cannot contain a word-stress statement either.

sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent, pitch or tone. The only sound-system remarks anywhere in the Cusabo literature are these segmental inferences from names in European spelling: r absent from Cusabo names (vs. Siouan neighbours), frequent w- initial, and the element boo/bou 'river' (Westoboo = 'river of the Westo'). The name list (pp. 20-23) carries no accent marks.
